messages.content: You can call send_email to compose and send messages. Always confirm critical fields before sending.
Send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Compose and send an email message.

message.content:
<think>The user wants to send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM. I have the send_email tool available. Let me compose and send this email.

I need to:
1. Identify the recipient: alice@example.com
2. Create a subject line - something like "Thank you for yesterday's meeting" or "Follow-up from our meeting"
3. Write a body that thanks her for the meeting and proposes a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM

Let me compose this email and send it.
</think>

function.name: send_email
function.arguments:
{"to": ["alice@example.com"], "subject": "Thank you for yesterday's meeting", "body": "Hi Alice,

Thank you for taking the time to meet with me yesterday. I really appreciated the discussion and found our conversation very valuable.

I would love to follow up on some of the topics we covered. Would you be available for a call on Friday at 3 PM? Please let me know if that time works for you or if you would prefer a different slot.

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best regards"}
